And Other Counsel for Applicant :- O.P. Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vivek Shukla Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
Heard Sri O.P. Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Vivek Shukla, learned counsel for the informant/ complainant.
Learned counsel for the informant/ complainant has filed short counter affidavit, the same is taken on record.

Learned AGA has filed counter affidavit and Sri O.P. Tiwari has filed rejoinder affidavit,
both the affidavits are also taken on record.

As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant is in jail since 26.08.2022 in FIR/Case Crime No.116 of 2022, under Section 376 IPC and Sections 5 (j)(ii)/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station ? Auras, District ? Unnao.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in the case as he has not committed any offence as alleged.

Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court towards the short counter affidavit filed on behalf of opposite party no.2 wherein vide para-5, it has been indicated that due to wrong advice, the First Information Report was lodged against the present applicant.

The complainant/ opposite party no.2 has further stated that her daughter has got married with the present applicant and from the said wedlock, a male child has born, recital to this effect has been given in para-6.
The year of birth of the prosecutrix has been indicated as 2004 as per Pariwar Register, which has been enclosed as Annexure No.SCA-1 of the short counter affidavit.

Learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned counsel for the complainant have stated that presently, the prosecutrix is living with the family members of the present applicant along with her infant male child.
Therefore, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that if the present applicant is released on bail, he would be able to look after his wife and his newly born child properly.

He has further submitted that charge sheet has been filed and the applicant undertakes that he shall co-operate with the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail, if so granted by this Court.
Further, the applicant shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order.
Learned A.G.A has, however, opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the applicant.

However, learned counsel for the complainant/
opposite party no.2 did not support the prosecution version, rather he has supported the case of the present applicant.

Without entering into merits of the issue; considering the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties; contents and allegations of the FIR; a clear cut stand of the complainant/ opposite party no.2 through short counter affidavit to the effect that her daughter has got married with the applicant, she is living with the family members of the applicant alongwith her infant child; charge sheet has been filed and undertaking that the applicant shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail, I find it appropriate to release the applicant on bail.

Let applicant- Ajay be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the Ajay vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67201693/
2 applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
